Use case: style-transfer. Repaint input 1 as one square rough hand-painted game martial card illustration for 致命穿刺.
Input 1 is the COMPOSITION TARGET: preserve the diagonal black spear shaft from upper left, the large pointed steel spearhead reaching lower right, the curved dark armor plate at lower left with its broken opening beneath the blade base, and a few heavy fragments suspended at upper right. Preserve the entirely visible point and connected weapon geometry. Keep the existing slate gray-blue/warm-charcoal broad rectangular painted background with pale surrounding negative space, simplifying its edges into broad deliberate brush strokes. Do not replace that background with an all-white cutout or invent a landscape. Input 2 (hero-summoner) is STYLE ONLY for opaque broad paint marks, quiet masses and selective edge detail. Input 3 (source-8) is STYLE ONLY for grouped dark masses and economical structural marks. Neither style reference contributes people, clothes, flowers or setting.
Make the action readable as one spear having just punched through a thick armor plate: the socket and blade emerge through one tight opening, two substantial torn lips bend outward with bright newly exposed metal edges and dark undersides, several separate fragments fly away. The broad triangular spearhead is a continuous coherent steel object with a central ridge and two decisive blade planes, one pale cold silver and one muted blue-gray. Give the puncture a compact deep crimson accent. Move the short crimson tassel from the far upper-left shaft end to the socket just behind the spearhead; let it stream backward up-left along the shaft in two broad trailing shapes. Preserve the weapon's diagonal, proportions and focal hierarchy. No visible human, hands, body or gore.

Hand-painted anime concept illustration built from large connected opaque color masses, a few wide directional swipes and blunt dabs. Each brush shape explains blade planes, curved armor volume and the force of the torn metal. Clear grouped light and shadow, decisive handmade edges, selective overlaps and broken stroke endings surrounded by quiet areas. Principal plate planes retain one or two broad curved midtone turns, a few crease or contour marks at the puncture and metal edges; large dark areas stay quiet. Material is described by broad flat silver highlights, muted reflected blue and warm gray shadow, not smooth chrome gradients or photographic reflections. Tassel consists of two or three broad red painted masses without fine threads. Concentrate richer red at the tie and puncture, with dark charcoal, steel blue and gray-white elsewhere. Foreground tip and the torn opening get the clearest edges; distant shaft and fragments use economical marks. Avoid tiny triangular mosaics, dense scratches, indiscriminate texture, glossy 3D, smooth airbrush, all-over grain or canvas filters, particle clouds and excessive ornament. Preserve selective handmade paint texture without covering every surface. No text, watermark, UI, border or extra weapons.
